item: The write gate's finally-path lost wake-up is forced by a test, and the claims of the wake-step change that no test or measurement backed are corrected
refs: follow-up to PR #1448 (independent read of its head); coordinator 17 Oct (option a)
summary: The read of the merged head of #1448 found that the comment, the lesson and the shipped row named the wake-up lost in the finally of an acquire that gave up as forced by the tests, and no test forced it. Two tests and an untimed control now interrupt the queue head in its wait on a free gate, fail the wake-up its finally owes, and require the writer behind it to get through; under the old untimed waits they fail on behaviour (checked by a mutant that restores them). Words corrected: the red-without sentences (the old waits with the constant defined fail on behaviour; the literal old module fails earlier at the setattr of the missing constant), the release test's name (its 5 s bound proves not for ever, not one step), the CPU line for the 917 s and 977 s holds (it needs 49 queued writers, whose number during those holds is not known), the loop quoted as written, and the pool-timeout aside (that 30 s is the connection-checkout timeout, not a gate wait). Found by the read and recorded in the original row: an acquire with a timeout of infinity or above the platform limit used to raise OverflowError from the wait after joining the queue. No source behaviour changes; one comment phrase in writer.py.
